notes.title: Small bug fixes, balancing tweaks, and cross platform support
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

We hope your summer is off to a fantastic start and that you're making the most of the Steam Summer Sale! We're thrilled to announce that TimeMelters will launch on PS5 on July 11th, and we've been working tirelessly to make it happen. The porting process has been an incredible journey, and doing it all in-house has taught us a lot, resulting in improved optimization on PC as well.

We're excited to share that the co-op mode will now feature cross-platform play with PS5, and you'll be able to use the PC Friend's Pass too! So, if you have friends on PC or PS5 who haven't tried the game yet, now is the perfect time to let them know.

The update includes bug fixes, further optimizations, and balance tweaks. Stay tuned for more updates, and thank you for your continued support!

And don't forget, TimeMelters is 40% off for a few more days during the Steam Summer Sale!

Cheers!

notes.title: Spanish language update and hotfix!
notes.content:
Hey everyone, we are releasing a hot fix for TimeMelters today that also includes the Spanish language update!

There were a few issues that sprung up on us that needed some quick addressing, but we decided to also include a few features and bug fixes that were ready for an upcoming patch. The Patch notes are:

The final video at the end of the game sometimes played more than once
People running Windows 11 and a duel monitor set up where running into issues with the mouse losing focus, or not being able to click on anything
We fixed a few small bugs in the challenges
We added the name of the coop player in certain areas of the game
Added Spanish language option 
Added up and down mouse wheel sensitivity for Spirit Sight
Other minor bugs and optimizations

We're up to 78 reviews on Steam with a 93% Positive rating, which is incredible. We also happened to be one of the top 10 rated games in 2024 with a Metacritic of 89!! We almost can't even believe it. So thank you all for the overwhelming support, and we will continue to making TimeMelters as good a game as it can be leading up to this console launch later this years.

notes.title: Patch 1.1 released!
notes.content:
Hey all, we hope you've been enjoying the post 1.0 launch as much as we have! There are a lot of great reviews coming in, which is incredible. It's also a lot of fun for us to see people playing, understanding and having fun while exploring TimeMelters.

We already have a post game patch that is ready to go live, mainly fixing a few little bugs here and there:

Buffed the Fire Storm perk, increasing the shots from a Fire Spirit on an Orb.
Added a ping icon for user feedback when you right click in coop
Added a video that shows REDACTED in Clawdenvale
Fixed a bug with the horizontal/vertical mouse sensitivity
Fixed a coop/controller bug, it would vibrate when it wasn't suppose to
Fixed a bug where the player couldn't move after summoning the void spirit
Fixed an issue where videos would randomly stop playing properly
Fixed a bug where players would still have a bit of agony mana left but could not use it
Increased mana in strategist in Kamorr
Fixed a coop bug when the client player uses spirit blast right when they rewind time
Fixed a bug in the solo campaign where the first Community Challenge was still locked after playing Lancestorm
Fixed a bug with the sky in Elfarness
Fixed a bug with some particles FX that would not scale properly
Fixed bugs with some vegetation assets
Rebalanced a few challenges
Fixed other minor bugs/issues
Minor optimizations

We wanted to get this patch out fast to fix some of these issues that popped up after launch, and we're happy with how quickly we were able to turn this around. Going forward, we are working on adding Spanish text to the game!

Thank you all again, TimeMelters wouldn't be where it is now without all of your help. We truly appreciate it more than you can ever know,

The AutoExec team

notes.title: VERSION 1.0 NOW AVAILABLE!
notes.content:
We are very excited to launch TimeMelters version 1.0 today! It's been an incredible journey for us so far. As a team of 3, we've been working on TimeMelters for over 6 years. TimeMelters has gone through a lot of iterations in that time, long before it was in anyone's hand. We grinded out our very first Kickstarter, successfully funding it with 48 hours to go. This initial success was just the beginning; TimeMelters was lucky enough to win some awards along the way, including 5 gold awards at NYX for categories such as Best Storytelling and Best Strategy Game, as well as the Technological Innovation and Public Choice awards at MIGS, and ultimately, being crowned the grand winner of the Ubisoft Indie Contest. We still can't believe how lucky we were to win all of these awards! 

Then, we had our first experiences with an Early Access title, which allowed us to engage directly with the community. The feedback we received during this period was instrumental in shaping the game and making it the best it could be. You have no idea how much the feedback we received helped us make a better game. Interacting with the community, expanding and improving TimeMelters with the help of everyone’s feedback, has been a cornerstone of our development process. The entire journey has been invaluable, and everything we’ve learned along the way makes our future projects that much better. 

So thank you all for helping us get here!

Just because TimeMelters is officially out now doesn't mean we are done! We will still be listening to your comments and provide more updates and fixes as time goes on! Not to mention the console release is going to creep up on us very quickly, so stay tuned for more.

Version 1.0 Patch Notes:

-Updated Act 1 tutorials for faster action and better flow
-Balance changes to the main campaign
-Updated controller support including more user customization
-Updated UI / Better user feedback / Bigger text
-New Challenges were added and some old ones were rebalanced
-Fixed synchronization issues in coop
-Some changes to the text to make the dialogue more fluid
-Lots of tiny bug fixes and polish
-General performance optimization
-New Demo was added to the Steam page

notes.title: A Major update (patch #6) is now LIVE... and so is the Soundtrack!
notes.content:
Hey everyone! 
First, today marks the release of the TimeMelters' Soundtrack! So why not give a listen to some amazing tracks composed by our friend Michel F. April while reading this post ;)  And, of course, feel free to share these links on your social media!

[url=https://open.spotify.com/album/6VUEsNV3S7xcSekGcO1bEg]https://open.spotify.com/album/6VUEsNV3S7xcSekGcO1bEg[/url]

[url=https://music.apple.com/us/album/timemelters-original-game-soundtrack/1672185767]https://music.apple.com/us/album/timemelters-original-game-soundtrack/1672185767[/url]

And now... the latest update for TimeMelters is LIVE (and it's a big one)! As we said with the previous posts, we've adjusted a lot of the first user experience in this update, so if you have been waiting to try out TimeMelters, now might be the time to jump in! Lots of changes, with many features added and fixes.  So without further ado, here are the patch notes:

-Revamped Lancestorm to teach spells/abilities and tutorials that are learned in Duskamble.
-Swapped around NewRisen and Duskamble in the mission order.
-Revamped Duskamble to include time rewind.
-Storyline adjustments to reflect the changes in the first 4 missions.
-Switched around a few spots for when spells perks are given out.
-Reworked teleport ability controls. PRESSING T always sets a new teleport spot, HOLDING T will always teleport the player. Changed for consistency in controls, before it was flip flopping and confusing.
-Updated spells and abilities in the grimoire text to reflect control changes.
-Added pause on death feature to give the player more strategic options instead of auto rewind (toggle on and off in the options menu).
-Fixed a network issue in coop that some people in different regions around the world were having, which caused issues staying connected to each other.
-Fixed a network issue where people were unable to reconnect if one of the player's internet started to struggle.
-Fixed game objective issues and rebalanced some challenges in challenge mode.
-Fixed deterministic issues arising in a few levels.
-Fixed mission objectives in Brooden cliffs that were not behaving as expected.
-Miscellaneous bug fixed and optimizations.

There you have it! A few structural changes to the start of the game to help with the first user experience. Lancestorm is a lot more engaging now with the new spells and we get to play with the Time Rewind feature a bit sooner. In turn this makes Duskamble a lot more fun too because you get to play with time rewind also. 

The control changes for the Teleport ability were to erase a bit of confusion we were seeing. These changes should make the ability a bit easier to use for new comers, but anyone that's played the game before may take a little getting used to.

Pausing on death is an amazing feature, because now you can got into strategic view to get a better lay of the land before you decide to go back in time, or you can even teleport away to save the rewind if you choose (and have a teleport spot active).

We are incredibly happy with this update. It was a large undertaking but we really feel like this improves the experience so much. Please, give it a shot and let us know what you think in the Discord!

What we will be working over the next weeks:
1-Completely new UI (based on the feedback we've received these past few months).
2-Better "Challenges" and "Grimoire" integration in the flow of the game.
3-More optimizations/polish/balancing.
4-First attempts on porting the game to Xbox (fingers crossed)!
5-(and maybe... just maybe) A Friend's Pass, allowing someone who owns the game to play the Coop campaign with a friend.

Until then, have fun, and thanks everyone you all once again for all your amazing support!

The AutoExec team

notes.title: MAJOR UPDATE - FULL CONTROLLER SUPPORT!
notes.content:
Hey all,
Good news! We just launched a new update for TimeMelters and we wanted to give you a quick rundown of the patch notes. We also updated the demo to include controller support and all the QOL improvements we've been adding to the game with these last few updates.

- Full Controller Support! Every UI, game objective, and grimoire text change if you use a controller, and then change back if you use keyboard/mouse, 100% seamlessly. It will even detect the controller you're using and display the appropriate controls.
- We added clearer objectives and improved the UI based on your feedback and streamers we saw playing. This includes clearer controls for navigation in Spirit Sight/Strategic View and casting spells among other things.
- We reworked a lot of the sounds in the game, especially enemies. Levels are more even throughout and we tried to add more atmosphere in general.
- General bug fixes and balancing changes were made. Mostly challenges, and a few adjustments in the story campaign.
- Ultra wide support is complete (still in [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1096140/discussions/0/3542672490603820733/]+experimental mode[/url] because we want to do further testing, but should be 100% done now)

[url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1096140/discussions/0/3542672490603820733/]+experimental[/url] still includes 4k resolution and ultra settings as we are still optimizing the game.

Thanks again for all your continued support! 

Don't forget if you want to leave us some solid feedback, you can fill out this [url=https://forms.gle/EcSrDhQWRWwWmFXj6]Survey[/url]! 

Last little note, we created some new trailers highlighting a few content creators that played 

TimeMelters over the last month! You can check them out on the steam page, but we will be posting them elsewhere in the coming weeks. 

Thanks again to [url=https://www.youtube.com/@Kaiff]Kaif[/url], [url=https://www.youtube.com/@EbbzYT]Ebbz[/url] and [url=https://www.youtube.com/farfromsubtle]FarFromSubtle[/url] for playing our game and letting us have a bit of fun with your footage.

The AutoExec team

notes.title: Patch #2 is Live! Ultra wide and controller support pass#2 (Experimental Mode)
notes.content:
Hello all! 
  We've been working really hard this past few weeks to release our second patch.  Aside from bugs fixes and tweaks, we added a new "Dialog option", which allows the players to choose either a more "concise" version of the story, or a richer storyline with more dialogs and backstories (for players who like to read). 

We added A LOT more features in the Experimental Mode (see how to launch the game in that mode below). Now we've finished  "phase 2" of the controller support (about 80% of the UI has been redone to support PS, Xbox and a LOT more controllers). And you can switch from keyboard/mouse to controller at any time seamlessly!

Also, in the experimental mode, we now support Ultra Wide resolutions.  There are still 1 or 2 tutorial pop ups that need some fine tuning, but 99% of the game is fully playable in ultra wide now.

For the next patch, we aim to move the controller support and ultra wide mode out of the experimental branch., and focus some more on polish and optimizations.


REMINDER : To launch the game in experimental mode, do the following : 
1 - Right-Click on the name of the game in your Steam Library
2 - Click Properties
3 - In the General Tab, at the bottom, you'll see a field under "launch option". Simply type "+experimental" in that field.

Then, when you'll launch the game, you'll be able to see the controller support (with the standard button mapping) in the "controls" menu.

Now, here's a list of features and fixes you'll find in the patch : 

Fixed the namesh in Bannerfort so corrupted villagers don't go around anymore (thanks to Runko for pointing it out)

Adjusted the dialogue and included a new option to select regular story mode or extended story mode.

Fixed a UI bug in Duskamble Challenge 3: the UI to show the echo activity hides. This should not be for this challenge since it has a Time Rift.

Switch the VSync for a 60 FPS target frame rate

Fixed an issue at the end of Clawdenvale where allies (Bone Walkers/converted Corrupted) were not being removed and were present during the remaining scenes.

Fixed a bug with Spirit Blast during Drain Life.

In SpiritSight and Strategic view, added control UI for Placing a marker and moving faster.

In Hawkden, fixed the path of the middle sorceress, it was in the ground.

Added more supported controllers, with a more complete updated UI. Still missing a few places, so controller support stays in +experimental mode.

Brooden Cliffs: when the 1st thunder finishes. there was a weird white fog in the distance, this is fixed.
Sorrow Keep Day: SSP bug when you close the stone walls. Partly fixed, enemies react properly, but their path on the right still needs fixing.

Clawdenvale: fixed a performance issue with the 1st vision of Teagan.

In Sorrow Keep Night, removed the option to "Restart at save point" during the load screen.

Sorrow Keep Night: 1st conversation with the villager, Moved Amannan to the the left with Teagan in the dialog layout.

Duskamble: at the end of the mission, the teleport spot was not being erased. Fixed.

The name for the savegames of the two Sorrow Keep missions were the same, we don't know which is which. Fixed.

Bannerfort: If the player had one spirit left and we arrives to the end before Amannan, they could activate the cemetery before early. This was adjusted.

Clawdenvale: Fixed an issue where Fafnogh has a hard time reaching his destination to interact with the crazy villager.

In the Grimoire, fix an issue where the text wrapped around badly.

Made it impossible to remap keyboard keys with Joystick inputs.

Disabled player physics and navMeshClamp while teleporting to fix some teleport issues with the Void Spirit spell.

Fixed an issue when a player died at the same time as they cast infuse life on a graveyard.

Fixed an issue when casting void room in multiplayer as Edwin.

Change the Earth Spirit tutorial to make it clearer.

In Mistgrow, made it clearer that you need to time yourself with your Echoes to shoot the Death Breathers.

Adjusted dialogue in the world map text about Thodoros.

Modified Ardorr Woods so that players can't shoot (in co-op and solo) at enemies from the other side of the river.

Enlarged the BG of the grimoire to add Infestors.


That's it! 
Thanks again everyone for your incredible support and all your comments!
And if you do like the game, don't hesitate to leave a review on Steam, it really motivates us and helps us make a better game!

Cheers!

Autoexec Team

notes.title: Patch #1 and controller support, 4K and very high settings (Experimental Mode)
notes.content:
Hey everyone,
   It's been a crazy 2 weeks post Early Access Launch! We've been working on the first patch for TimeMelters, which we hope will fix all the bugs people have posted on Discord and the Steam forums, along with some balancing changes and a few experimental features. These features include partial controller support, 4k resolution and 3 "very high" settings (vegetation, sky, shadows) for the people that feel like their rig can handle it!

To launch the game in experimental mode and help us test out these features, do the following steps :

1 - Right-Click on the name of the game in your Steam Librairy
2 - Click Properties
3 - In the General Tab, at the bottom, you'll see a field under "launch option". Simply type "+experimental" in that field.

Then, when you'll launch the game, you'll be able to see the controller support (with the standard button mapping) in the "controls" menu.  If you prefer a different button mapping, you can create your own using the Steam controller interface or download a controller profile from the community. 

You'll also be able to play the game in 4K and try out the "very high" settings.  Please keep in mind that we are still working heavily on these features and, depending on your feedback and bug reports, we'll see if they can make it to version 1.0 .

So, here's a list of what you find in Patch 1.0 that is out today.

- Added a 3rd challenge in Callaburgh called "The Perfect Perk" and a new Steam Achievement
- Fixed a teleport issue some players reported when using the Void Spirit spell
- Experimental mode (add "+experimental" in the launch option to unlock it) adding controller support and allowing to run the game in 4K with very high settings
- Fixed some shader issues where the water plane was not showing properly
- Fixed a lot of collisions where players pass through objects
- And of course, a LOT of optimizations, fine tunings, typos and balancing based on your feedback and comments

It's been a pleasure reading what everyone has to say, you have no idea! If you've given TimeMelters a shot, please leave us a comment, it really helps us make a better game! 

Thank you all again, we wouldn't have made it without you!

Happy gaming!

notes.title: TimeMelters is NOW available in Early Access!
notes.content:
Hello all!
  TimeMelters is finally out on Steam! We've been working on TimeMelters for a solid 5 years and to reach this point is incredible. The game is in Early Access, so please, if you have any feedback for us, comments/ideas or you found some bugs, let us know in the Steam forums/Discord or send us an email at support@autoexecgames.com.
 
If you haven't had the chance to try out TimeMelters yet, we hope you enjoy it as much as we enjoyed making it. It was a labour of love, and we honestly can not wait to see what sort of strategies people come up with using our systems,

Happy gaming!

The AutoExec team
